title: August 28, 2026
summary: New: keep multiple AI chats on one study and switch between them from the top bar; the study workspace adds dedicated Setup, Results, and Report tabs with a shareable report URL; report highlight reels can now stitch multiple clips into a single video; the researcher chat can read your study report. Improved: reports place charts and reels inline beside the findings they support, draw on your research plan, and are easier to scan with scaled headings, numbered citations, and an evidence carousel; AI-moderated sessions resume after a dropped connection; the sidebar remembers its collapsed state. Fixed: sub-steps can be removed from the workflow outline; moderation waits for prototypes to load; device-setup speech is kept out of transcripts; background moderation hiccups no longer mark sessions as no-shows; voice defaults off outside AI-moderated studies; report evidence slideouts focus the clicked theme; new chats show their title without a refresh; teammates' studies no longer replay the research goal as a first chat message.
body_markdown:
### New


- You can now keep multiple AI chats on a single study and switch between them, or start a fresh one, from the top bar. Each conversation keeps its own history, so you can explore different questions without losing a thread. (AI Assistant)
- The study workspace now has dedicated **Setup** , **Results** , and **Report** tabs, and the report has its own URL. Reloads and shared links land on the right tab instead of resetting to the study. (Study Templates & Methods)
- Report highlight reels can now stitch multiple clips into a single video, so a[reel](https://greatquestion.co/support/repository/reels) built from several moments plays as one continuous asset. (Repository)
- The researcher chat can now read your study report, so you can ask follow-up questions about findings and evidence without leaving the conversation. (AI Assistant)


### Improved


- Reports now place computed charts and highlight reels inline beside the findings they support, instead of collecting them in the appendix. (Repository)
- The report writer now draws on your study's research plan and on expert researcher feedback, so findings are framed around your goals, research questions, and success criteria. (Repository)
- Reports are easier to scan: headings scale by level, finding headlines are numbered, inline citations render as numbered reference pills, and detailed evidence pages through a carousel instead of a long scroll. (Repository)
- [AI-moderated](https://greatquestion.co/support/studies/ai-moderation) sessions now resume after a dropped connection, so participants pick up where they left off instead of losing the moderator's response. (Participant Experience)
- The navigation sidebar now remembers whether you collapsed it, even after a reload. (Platform & Integrations)


### Fixed


- You can now remove sub-steps from a study's workflow outline. (Study Templates & Methods)
- In[AI-moderated prototype tests](https://greatquestion.co/support/studies/ai-moderated-prototype-testing) , moderation now waits until the prototype has finished loading before asking the participant to begin. (Participant Experience)
- Speech during device setup no longer appears in the session transcript. (Participant Experience)
- Background moderation hiccups no longer mark otherwise-successful sessions as no-shows. (Participant Experience)
- Voice responses now default to off for studies that aren't AI-moderated. (Participant Experience)
- Clicking a theme's evidence in a report now opens the slideout focused on that theme, with the question's other themes behind a toggle. (Repository)
- New chats now show their generated title without a page refresh. (AI Assistant)
- Opening a teammate's study no longer replays the research goal as the first chat message. (AI Assistant)
